empty-choices: Treat an explicit empty choices list as a valid upstream response, including in shared dictionary-to-response conversion, sync/async conversion to streaming, stream response construction and the Anthropic compatibility adapter. Return an empty choices list without raising APIError or IndexError and without fabricating an assistant choice. Preserve usage-only responses. Missing choices and choices of the wrong type (including null) remain malformed and should raise APIError with a useful diagnostic identifying choices and the supplied type. Existing tests that deliberately reject [] encode the old behavior and must be updated for this change.
anthropic-image-guardrail: Anthropic message guardrails drop image blocks whose source type is url. Forward URL sources as URL strings, including images nested in tool results. For base64 sources with media_type, supply a data URL preserving that MIME type; keep raw base64 as a fallback when media_type is absent. Ignore malformed sources and unsupported file sources. Preserve the original message content.
databricks-reasoning: Databricks chat responses can carry thinking in reasoning_content, its reasoning alias, structured reasoning content blocks, or <think> tags inside string content. Preserve reasoning_content and visible answer text in normal and streaming responses, including reasoning-only chunks. Existing structured reasoning blocks take precedence over top-level fields. A string with <think> tags must separate reasoning from the visible answer. Preserve existing tool and citation behavior.
openai-schema-patterns: Tool schema pattern values rejected by Python re compilation cause OpenAI request failures. Remove incompatible pattern constraints recursively in schema positions across OpenAI and Azure Chat and Responses, including custom OpenAI API bases, compact requests and namespace tools. Preserve other schema properties and valid Python regexes. Preserve existing combinator flattening behavior: routes that currently retain unions must keep them. Non-OpenAI providers must retain their patterns. Do not mutate caller-owned tool schemas. Data values in default/const/enum/examples are not schema constraints. Deep or invalid patterns should not crash request conversion.
databricks-unity: Databricks Unity model service names are dotted catalog.schema.model names (at least two dots after the optional databricks/ prefix). Preserve that full name in the request body and route it through /ai-gateway/mlflow/v1/chat/completions. Convert a bare workspace host or legacy /serving-endpoints base to that gateway path. Preserve explicitly configured gateway bases and custom non-legacy paths without doubling slashes. Ordinary model names must retain existing serving-endpoint routing and authentication behavior.
mai-image-params: Correct Azure AI MAI image request mapping. Image editing accepts prompt, image, model and n, with multipart field image; size is unsupported and must either raise an HTTP 400 unsupported-parameter error or be omitted when drop_params is enabled, without injecting a default size. Image generation supports exactly one image: reject n other than 1 (including non-numeric values) with HTTP 400, or drop unsupported n when per-call/global drop_params is enabled. Convert generation size strings to width and height; require each dimension >=768 and total pixels <=1,056,768. Invalid formats and unsupported parameters must surface as HTTP 400. Explicit provider width/height parameters remain pass-through. Keep the model in the JSON body, existing MAI routing, configured endpoint paths, and flat per-image pricing fallback.
bedrock-thinking: Bedrock Converse incorrectly advertises and forwards Anthropic-shaped thinking parameters to DeepSeek models. DeepSeek R1 reasons natively and rejects both thinking and reasoning_effort. DeepSeek V3 accepts raw reasoning_effort but does not accept the Anthropic thinking field. Reflect this in advertised supported parameters, normal unsupported-parameter errors, drop_params behavior, and direct request mapping so rejected fields never leak through. Recognize both model identifiers and resolved base model identifiers. Preserve existing reasoning request mapping for Claude, Nova, OpenAI and other non-DeepSeek models.
team-router-names: Resolve a team-scoped auto-router by its public name consistently in strategy dispatch, candidate deployment lookup and pre-call compression. Team requests may use only that team's router; another team must not reach its strategy or marker parameters. A team-specific public name shadows a global model only for that team. Select tag-scoped marker deployments matching original request tags, then an untagged fallback; never use a marker scoped to other tags as the fallback. Markers describe a strategy and are not callable deployments: reject marker-only resolutions. Forward the selected marker's allowed parameters, and choose callable tier deployments. An admin without a team may resolve a uniquely named team router, but a name shared across teams is ambiguous. Compression policy must use the same resolution and be installed before guardrails.
router-retry-deployment: When a deployment refuses a request and RetryPolicy permits another attempt (including BadRequestError/HTTP 400), retries must move to another eligible deployment. Carry the failed deployment identity through the exception into the existing retry exclusion mechanism across completion, text completion, embeddings, images, speech, transcription, rerank, search, Responses and pass-through entrypoints, for sync and async variants where supported. Ensure selectors receive request retry exclusions. Preserve fallback behavior and ordinary non-retried errors. Do not require a new helper name: correctness is assessed through existing request entrypoints.
